name: John Glenn Columbus International Airport
before:
Columbus's airport, 6 miles east of downtown, with 148 non-stop flights a day to 31 airports.

One thing matters more than anything else here. The three concourses are not connected airside. Each has its own security checkpoint, so moving between them means leaving security and clearing again. A client connecting between airlines in different concourses needs to know that before they arrive.

Concourse A has 7 gates and is mainly Southwest. Concourse B has 16 gates for American, Air Canada and United. Concourse C has 11 gates for Alaska, Breeze, Delta, Frontier and Sun Country, and is also where international arrivals without pre-clearance are processed.

The code CMH comes from Columbus Municipal Hangar, the airport's original name. It was renamed in 2016 after John Glenn, the astronaut and four-term senator.
after:
Columbus's main airport, 6 miles east of downtown. The airport says 11 airlines fly nonstop to 53 destinations.

One thing matters more than anything else here. The three concourses are not connected airside. Each has its own security checkpoint, so moving between them means leaving security and clearing again. A client connecting between airlines in different concourses needs to know that before they arrive.

Southwest uses Concourse A, while American and United use Concourse B. The airport lists Air Canada, Alaska, Breeze, Delta, Frontier and Sun Country in Concourse C.

It was called Port Columbus International Airport until 2016, when it was renamed after John Glenn, the astronaut and senator.

claims.note: Was 'Columbus's airport'. 'Main' added because Columbus has a second airport with scheduled passenger flights, Rickenbacker (Allegiant only), run by the same authority. The FAA's 2025 table has 4,396,625 boardings here against 170,808 at Rickenbacker.
